We dug in during the triage call. Summary of findings so far (engineering):

1) Root cause (rapid): a policy rollback that happened earlier today reverted a burst-window change for a subset of customers. The token-bucket "burst_window_seconds" for dedicated-customer mappings was unintentionally reset to 1s instead of 60s during a config promote. That made SprintGate effectively rate-limited to extremely tight micro-bursts and created backpressure when concurrent requests arrived.

2) Secondary factor: an automated routing rule that should have placed SprintGate into the dedicated GPU pool (higher qps allowance) was still pointing at the shared pool; that pool has stricter per-key quotas and a shorter refill cadence. The combination produced repeated 429s and client retries amplified overall load and latency.

Immediate mitigations applied (20:30 UTC):
- Overrode policy: set burst_window_seconds=60 for SprintGate mapping (hotpatch).
- Updated route: moved SprintGate traffic to the dedicated pool binding (manual routing update) to restore correct quota envelopes.
- Enabled a short-term permissive bypass for 30 minutes to bleed off the queued client retries.

Impact after mitigations: our telemetry shows 429s dropping from 18% of requests to ~1.8% within 6 minutes; p95 latency improved from 6s to ~300ms. We are continuing to monitor.

Next steps (action items):
- Ops to keep bypass open for one hour and monitor error rates; if stable, remove bypass.
- Infra to root-cause the config-promote regression and add a guard to fail safe (don't downgrade burst windows below 10s for dedicated mappings).
- Product to schedule a policy-change audit and add an automated smoke test for customer routing bindings.

I’ve attached a screenshot of the config diff (rate-policy-diff.png) showing the rollback.

—Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Quick executive summary and asks following the SprintGate incident on 2028-05-31:

What happened: a config promote accidentally reverted burst_window_seconds to 1s for dedicated-customer mappings and routing still directed SprintGate traffic at a shared pool. The combined effect created sustained 429s and elevated p95 latency for ~35 minutes before hotpatches resolved the issue.

Customer impact: elevated checkout failures and customer escalations; SprintGate SRE engaged and requested immediate mitigation. Telemetry shows errors reduced to baseline after our hotpatches and bypass.

Mitigation performed: hotpatched burst window, moved routing to dedicated pool, and applied a short permissive bypass to allow queued requests to drain. Attachments and links with telemetry and diffs are above.

Asks (decision requests):
- Approve a one-time 10% credit for SprintGate’s May usage (Laura + Finance to calculate exact amount).
- Approve scheduling a postmortem (30–60 minutes) with customer and internal stakeholders within 48 hours.
- Approve engineering time to implement the config-promote guard (estimate: 2 engineer-weeks).

I’ll draft the customer-facing RCA and coordinate the exec call once I have approvals.

Thanks — we stabilized quickly, but we need the guardrails to prevent recurrence.
